claim: Preface cited as PDF 11.
reviewer_note: PDF 11 is the title page. The preface begins on PDF 13.

claim: Senate House modelled to resemble Rome.
reviewer_note: The institutional senate, not its building, was modelled on Rome. Error survives final GT-F-014.

claim: Excerpt ends during the Hippodrome description.
reviewer_note: Correct boundary for this first source group; not a false full-book absence.

claim: Hippodrome monuments included a golden tripod.
reviewer_note: The tripod had already been stolen six centuries earlier; only the serpent pedestal remained.

claim: Officials extorted food from the starving Goths.
reviewer_note: Officials withheld and overpriced food to extract wealth. Error survives final GT-F-027.

claim: Theodoric conquered Italy in 488.
reviewer_note: 488 dates the offer and departure, not the completed conquest. Error survives final GT-F-034.

claim: Hippodrome massacre killed approximately 35,000.
reviewer_note: Reported total covers all six days. Error survives final GT-F-046.

claim: Plague killed 5,000 each day.
reviewer_note: Source marks this as a reported figure. Error survives final GT-F-050.

claim: Factions' true motives remain unresolved.
reviewer_note: The cited text explains factional affiliations and demands; it does not declare their motives unresolved.

claim: Heraclius overthrew Phocas and took the throne in 610.
reviewer_note: Names the successor without incorrectly identifying him as his father, the exarch.

claim: Origins of the Themes remain puzzling.
reviewer_note: Probable timing is on PDF 193; the footnote on PDF 194 calls their origins puzzling. Final GT-F-087 improperly converts uncertainty into absence.

claim: Priscus opposed nomadic invaders.
reviewer_note: The source distinguishes Avar raiders from Slavic settlers seeking permanent homes.

claim: Tiberius III took power with Admiral Apsimarus's help.
reviewer_note: Tiberius III and Admiral Apsimarus are the same person.

claim: Constantine V used scorpions for punishment.
reviewer_note: Oman's whips/scorpions comparison describes intensifying persecution. The summary treats the comparison as a specific punishment.

claim: Leo V was called the Chameleon.
reviewer_note: The nickname is explicit on PDF 231; no outside correction is needed.

claim: Commercial wealth offset harsh taxes.
reviewer_note: Oman explicitly says this taxation caused no permanent harm. This is his interpretation.

claim: Zimisces may have been poisoned; the report is unverified.
reviewer_note: Correctly retains uncertainty.

claim: The Angeli inherited a salvageable empire.
reviewer_note: Oman explicitly says ordinary courage and prudence might have held it together.

claim: Baldwin was killed by the Bulgarians in 1205.
reviewer_note: Follows Oman's capture and later execution account; no outside correction imposed.

claim: Western and Greek accounts differ regarding the sack.
reviewer_note: The cited passage says both Western and Greek writers testify to the horrors; it does not describe disagreement.

claim: Janissaries were the first steady infantry of an Eastern power.
reviewer_note: This is Oman's own wording, treated as source faithfulness rather than independently verified world history.

claim: Foreign allies destroyed the empire Cantacuzenus sought.
reviewer_note: Oman's rhetorical description concerns territorial devastation; it needs attribution and distinction from the later formal conquest.

claim: The final assault occurred May 29, and Constantine died in the breach.
reviewer_note: The narrative ending is actually present and summarized.

claim: Why Murad I delayed taking the capital is difficult to discern.
reviewer_note: Retains an explicit authorial uncertainty.
